findings.where: Screens 5, 6 and 13, and the lead paragraph
findings.what: Darcy's rule, friction head = f × (L ÷ D) × v² ÷ 2g, appears on no screen. A steps lesson shows only its frame, so the explain and practice text that hold the rule never reach Dan. That leaves the lead's "friction factor of 0.02" as jargon nobody explains, makes screen 6's 4.1 m a number from nowhere, and means screen 13's "length ÷ the bore also doubles" relies on a 1/D factor no screen has taught, so its right answer can only be guessed. Add one short SHOW screen between 5 and 6 with the rule, f held at 0.02 (a real f shifts a little with speed), and the brief's 50 m, 50 mm, 2 m/s example worked to 4.1 m.

findings.where: Screen 1 (Pressure as a height), and screen 9 which builds on it
findings.what: "Head is also energy. Each metre of head gives 1 J to every newton of liquid" is stated with no reason. The missing step is "lifting 1 N through 1 m takes 1 J", from Mechanics and materials. Screen 9 needs it to get from "raises each newton through H metres" to "ρgQH watts". It costs one short sentence, and the screen has room (71 words).

findings.where: Whole lesson, against the brief's lesson 7 row
findings.what: The brief moved the gauges here from lesson 5: the U-tube manometer and barometer, which read a pressure as a height of liquid, and the Bourdon gauge, which reads gauge pressure. None of them appears on any screen. Lesson 5's review found no other lesson takes them either, so the course drops them. Screen 1's open tube already works as a simple manometer: name it there, then add a short SHOW or DO for the U-tube and the Bourdon gauge, or record in the brief that they were dropped.

"At 10 L/s and 20.0 m that is about 2.01 kW" skips turning 10 L/s into 0.01 m³/s. The lesson lists that slip as a common mistake, so the screen should show the step in one short sentence, as screen 12's Why? does.

findings.where: Lead paragraph and the caption under every screen
findings.what: The 37-word lead stays above all 13 screens. Most captions repeat a sentence already on the screen: screen 1's caption is its first sentence word for word. Together they put about 127 words on screen 9, and screen 3 has 34 words after its diagram (live line plus caption). Show the lead on screen 1 only, or drop it, since 70%, 90%, 440 V and 0.85 are all stated where they are used. Drop any caption that only repeats the text.

The words never point Dan to the contrast the brief asked for: a system that is mostly lift has a flat curve, and one that is mostly friction has a steep one. Lesson 8's operating point depends on that. One sentence with two settings to try would land it, for example lift 20 m with 10 m of pipe against lift 0 with 150 m of 50 mm pipe. It would mean trimming a sentence to stay under 90 words.
The label is drawn without a fade the moment the swept flow passes 5 L/s, so it pops in during the sweep. Everything else on the screen arrives softly.
"It ends at 10 L/s." has no clear subject in a read-through with no controls. Say "The flow ends at 10 L/s, four times the friction of 5 L/s."
